title.analysis: Authentic title "You're Not Ready For What's Coming" is a vague, ominous warning with no subject noun. The script delivers a 50-minute macro-household survey (stagnant real income, tariffs, debt, AI layoffs, retirement, housing, recession risk, psychology) and a five-step action plan. The promise is broad enough to be met. It performed TYPICAL against a cohort where the concrete-topic housing title ("WTF Just Happened To The Housing Market?!") is the large outlier. Association only.

thumbnail.analysis: Registered maxresdefault 1280x720 (HTTP 200, real image). White background. The recurring cartoon man (grey T-shirt), mouth open, points at an easel chart: a green rising line, then a red crashing arrow with "2026" in red. A heavy black headline reads "IT'S HAPENING!", MISSPELLED (one P), with a curved arrow to the chart. At 320x180 the headline, face and crash arrow stay legible, so the typo is visible at mobile size. It signals a market crash, while the script hedges ("nobody knows with confidence", "the right move has never been to exit"), so the packaging is more alarmist than the content.

script.stored_text_completeness: All 42635 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; long-form (2,984 s, 7,292 words); full stored text read in one pass; stored ending is complete with sign-off ("you'll want to be here for it."); ASR garbles ("$160" for $160 billion card interest; "On 70%"; "Demos calculated that over a full career for 401k fees"; "is not a exception as if it were a natural law"); fillers minor; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: You're standing at the grocery store checkout. The cashier reads out your total, $318. You look down at the cart, same chicken, same bread, same stuff you've bought every week for 3 years. You stand there for a second doing the math in your head. It used to be $210. You didn't add anything. Nothing in your life got more expensive on purpose, but but somehow that number keeps going up every single month and your paycheck, which you did
script.ending_words: knew. You're watching this video, you paid attention to this for 50 minutes, which means you already know more than most people. The only question now is what you do with it. If this changed something for you, drop a comment and tell me what the first move is. Subscribe if you want to keep thinking about this stuff. There's more coming and you'll want to be here for it.
script.analysis: Full 42635 canonical characters read. A long-form composite-character essay: grocery-checkout hook; flat real median income vs prices; Elijah and real wages; shrinkflation; tariffs (Vietnam shoes, Yale, NY Fed pass-through); Isabella and card, auto and student debt; depleted savings and BNPL; Luna and AI layoffs, U-6, the benchmark revision, Challenger, Klarna; Calyx and retirement math, 401(k) fees, Social Security depletion, 401(k) history; Jordan and Alex and housing lock-in; recession odds and fiscal room; psychology (normalcy bias, anchoring, doom spending, loss aversion); action plan (emergency fund, debt, keep investing, HSA, housing math, Roth conversions); two-futures close. Verified: Census income, Yale tariff cost, NY Fed 94% (Jan-Aug 2025), NY Fed card balances, SF Fed excess savings, NAHB 74.9%, Challenger AI cuts, DOL fee example, retirement arithmetic. Wrong or misattributed: 2026 401(k)/HSA limits (all four), the 22.5% tariff rate credited to the Tax Foundation, "10% smaller" labour market, 2009 home-sales comparison, Goldman/JPMorgan 65%, Klarna framing, stale 3.7% Morningstar rate. Unsupported: 30.9% panic sellers, 12.7% 90+ delinquency stock, the version-two outcomes. Several Edmunds values approximate but do not match Q4 2025. The stored ending is complete.

topic.analysis: A macro-to-household survey of 2025-26 financial pressure (stagnant real income, tariffs, debt, AI job loss, retirement shortfall, housing lock-in, recession risk) with a defensive action plan.
topic.audience_problem: Working households who feel worse off despite good headline data and want to know what to do.
topic.time_sensitivity: High: tariffs, labour data, 2026 limits and recession odds date quickly; several figures already stale or wrong at upload.
topic.narrative_angle: The floor moved, it is math not you; act early from stability.
topic.novelty_and_corpus_angle: Test a long-form "what is changing" video that keeps the composite-character structure and checks every dated figure against its primary release (2026 IRS limits, Morningstar rate, Edmunds quarter, Challenger totals), and fix the thumbnail typo.
topic.competition: Same-channel nearest-age peers in K01; not an independent niche or causal test

virality.analysis: Frozen 11367 views / 156.0207 days = 72.85572 views/day. Against 10 peers 0.77667x (TYPICAL); against 5 peers 1.11507x (TYPICAL). TYPICAL against ten peers (0.777x) and five peers; see observed_result for exact values. The cohort includes one large housing outlier (361K views), which raises the mean but not the median. An alarmist generic title and a misspelled crash thumbnail produced a median outcome. Association only; impressions and CTR unknown.

virality.competition: Exact same-channel/format/snapshot peer cohorts and thresholds in K01
